The system exhibits a wiring asymmetry: the index is fully built and queryable, yet the reasoning engine lacks consumption pathways. This creates a knowledge storage artifact rather than a knowledge integration layer. The retrieval quality regression signals a semantic drift in the index post-rebuild, indicating that while indexing is functional, the engine's ability to extract and reason over retrieved data is compromised. The presence of retracted records further complicates trustworthiness. The core failure lies in the disconnection between \( \mathcal{I} \) and \( \mathcal{R} \), where \( \mathcal{I} \) is the indexed corpus and \( \mathcal{R} \) is the reasoning module. This disjunction implies that even if \( \mathcal{I} \) is accurate and complete, \( \mathcal{R} \) will remain oblivious unless explicitly wired.
